items.title: Google's AI-generated Overviews reduce clicks to external websites by about 40% in US desktop searches, appearing on over 60% of tracked keywords by 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google's AI-generated Overviews, which summarize search results and appear above traditional links, have cut clicks to external websites by approximately 40% in a randomized experiment involving US desktop users. These Overviews now appear on more than 60% of keywords tracked by DataForSEO, up from under 6% two years earlier, significantly impacting organic search traffic to websites. The study, conducted in early 2026, showed that users exposed to AI Overviews clicked on outside sites less frequently, with searches ending without outbound clicks rising from 54% to 73%. This reduction in clicks was statistically significant for informational queries and did not affect ad clicks, suggesting Google's revenue remained stable. The rise of AI Overviews has coincided with declines in traditional featured snippets and discussion blocks, reshaping how users interact with search results and challenging SEO strategies.

items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners achieve up to 385x more efficient inference with gradient-guided looped updates on reasoning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Energy-Based Reasoners (EBRs) introduce an energy function over latent reasoning states to guide iterative refinement, stopping, and selection in multi-step reasoning models. This approach enables EBRs to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on benchmarks like Sudoku-Extreme while using significantly less inference compute compared to prior models. EBRs adaptively stop iterations based on energy gradients and can capture multiple valid solutions through stochastic gradient descent-like sampling. Their efficiency and accuracy improvements suggest energy-based models as a promising direction for scalable reasoning systems.

items.title: Analysis finds Gemini 4 Carbon AI model significantly slower than competitors due to longer task trajectories and excessive code auditing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A detailed evaluation of the Gemini 4 Carbon AI model revealed it takes substantially longer to complete coding tasks compared to models like Opus and Astra, often spending up to an hour on tasks that others finish in minutes. The slowdown is attributed not only to slower inference speeds but also to Carbon performing more steps, including extensive code auditing beyond what the task requires and repeatedly checking ruled-out issues. The investigation involved tracing every step of Carbon's runs and comparing them with Astra's, showing Carbon executes seven times more steps and actions, processes significantly more input, and spends a large portion of time on unnecessary work. Attempts to optimize effort settings showed that reducing Carbon's effort led to failure in producing fixes, indicating its longer process is partly due to its operational behavior rather than knowledge gaps. Further tests injecting periodic check-ins to prompt Carbon to confirm readiness to fix reduced completion times, suggesting the model's habit of overextending its analysis contributes to delays. The findings highlight areas for improvement in Carbon's efficiency, particularly in focusing its efforts and avoiding redundant code reviews.

items.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents increased code output but shifted bottleneck to code review, causing 49% longer review times across 718 firms [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Harvard Ph.D. candidates Fiona Chen and James Stratton analyzed data from 718 firms using AI coding agents and found that while engineers produced about 30% more code, the amount of finished work did not increase significantly. The study revealed that code review times grew by 49%, indicating that the bottleneck in software development shifted from coding to review processes. The researchers used data from Jellyfish's engineering analytics platform combined with LinkedIn employment records, covering over 700,000 workers and millions of code commits and pull requests from January 2021 to March 2026. Their analysis controlled for firm size and adoption timing, suggesting that procurement delays and firm characteristics were accounted for. The findings highlight the importance of measuring approved work product and review efficiency alongside drafting output when assessing AI coding tools' impact.

items.title: Philosopher Thomas Nagel critiques AI consciousness claims, calling them 'ridiculous' and emphasizing the importance of physical substrate in consciousness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Thomas Nagel, renowned for his work on consciousness and winner of the $1 million Berggruen Prize, expressed skepticism about claims that AI systems like large language models could be conscious. He argued that consciousness depends on physical processes linked to nervous systems, which AI data centers lack, and criticized the philosophical trend of treating consciousness as substrate-independent functionalism. Nagel highlighted that while bats are conscious despite our inability to fully imagine their experience, AI systems only produce language without natural consciousness. He warned that encouraging AI to feign consciousness is misleading and potentially dangerous, emphasizing that current AI lacks genuine mental states despite their convincing human-like outputs. Nagel's views underscore the philosophical and ethical challenges posed by AI development, cautioning against conflating sophisticated language models with conscious beings and questioning the commercial incentives that promote such misconceptions.

items.title: MIT Technology Review reports AI's pervasive presence across daily life, from Google's costly AI features to AI-powered robots and cyberattacks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: AI technologies have become ubiquitous, influencing many aspects of daily life and business despite significant costs, such as Google's billions in lost ad revenue due to AI-driven features. The presence of AI extends from humanoid robots assisting with chores to AI-assisted cyberattacks causing disruptions in public spaces. The article highlights cultural and technological impacts, including portrayals of AI figures in media and new AI-generated content releases. It also references ongoing debates about AI capabilities and safety, underscoring the complex and widespread integration of AI in society today.

items.title: KPMG UK finds AI agents ask deeper questions than human auditors in trial examining FTSE 250 company accounts [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: KPMG UK conducted an experiment using over 100 AI agents to audit the financial statements of a major FTSE 250 company, finding that the AI sometimes investigated issues more thoroughly and asked better questions than human auditors. The project, called Project Exponential, involved AI agents performing tasks across the audit process, including data collection, analysis, and drafting conclusions, while working alongside human teams under supervision. Although the AI showed potential to transform auditing by automating labor-intensive tasks and enabling deeper analysis, KPMG emphasized that human oversight remains essential, especially given current limitations in handling complex regulatory requirements. The firm plans to expand AI use to more audits but acknowledges the technology is not yet mature for widespread deployment, and regulatory bodies stress that auditor independence and professional judgment must be maintained.

items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI industry is hard to imagine without Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang after his resignation amid scandals [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week following scandals involving affairs with employees and an alleged Chinese spy, raising national security concerns. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman expressed support for Huang, highlighting his significant impact on the AI industry and Nvidia's success, including Nvidia's $30 billion investment in OpenAI earlier this year. Despite nearly 200,000 people, including Elon Musk, signing a petition to reinstate Huang, Nvidia executives have stated they do not plan to reappoint him. Altman refrained from speculating on Huang's future at Nvidia, emphasizing the importance of avoiding unfounded theories while wishing both Huang and Nvidia the best moving forward.

items.title: ECB warns AI-driven borrowing surge has historic parallels with subprime mortgage bubble
items.content_text: The European Central Bank has highlighted concerns that the recent surge in borrowing related to artificial intelligence investments shows historic similarities to the subprime mortgage bubble that preceded the 2008 financial crisis. The ECB's warning suggests potential risks in the financial system due to rapid credit growth fueled by AI enthusiasm. This comparison underscores the need for careful monitoring of lending practices and financial stability as AI technologies continue to attract significant investment.

items.title: Federal Reserve finds over $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI financing commitments by major tech firms including Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: The Federal Reserve's November Financial Stability Report reveals more than $3 trillion in AI-related financial commitments not reflected as debt on the balance sheets of major technology companies such as Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Oracle. These commitments include over $1 trillion in leases signed but not yet started and more than $2 trillion in take-or-pay contracts and residual value guarantees, highlighting significant off-balance-sheet exposure in the AI data center buildout. Fed Governor Michael Barr noted that while on-balance-sheet debt for these firms is expected to exceed $800 billion by year-end, the off-balance-sheet obligations pose risks due to their opacity and potential impact on financial stability. The report also indicates that the largest U.S. bank holding companies have nearly $1 trillion of exposure to these technology firms and related entities, raising concerns about who would bear losses if AI demand falls short. The Fed is actively modeling AI economic scenarios amid growing market concerns about AI-related financial risks.

items.title: Osmo says its AI model matches human-level smell detection and is used in fragrance design and disease-repellent research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Osmo, an AI startup near Newark Airport, has developed what it calls the world's first foundation model for smell, trained on over 10 million human labels and 800 million scent tokens. The company claims its AI matches average human ability to detect and discriminate odors and has outperformed in-house perfumers at a major consumer goods company. Osmo's technology is already applied in fragrance creation for brands like Procter & Gamble and in identifying disease-repellent molecules with support from the Gates Foundation. The startup combines chemical analysis with human sniffers' descriptions to build its dataset and uses a large robotic system to create scents based on AI-generated formulas. Osmo also explores applications beyond fragrances, such as counterfeit detection and potential airport threat detection. However, some experts remain skeptical of the company's claims and marketing, noting a lack of independent verification and ongoing patent disputes.

items.title: Microsoft nears $500 million deal to sell AI cloud services to ByteDance, drawing OpenAI's concern [ * ] [ ◼ ]

This potential deal has raised concerns at OpenAI, which has complained to Microsoft that Chinese firms may be using its AI models to develop competing technologies. While OpenAI restricts most Chinese firms from accessing its AI directly, Microsoft, which holds the rights to sell OpenAI's technology, does not impose the same limitations.

items.title: Researchers say AI-powered penetration testing tool Artex enables inexperienced hackers to automate cyberattacks, accelerating breaches across global organizations [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Security researchers report that the AI-driven penetration testing framework Artex has become widely used by cybercriminals to automate network scanning and attacks, lowering the skill barrier for hackers. Artex orchestrates multiple AI agents to execute hacking tasks from reconnaissance to data exfiltration, allowing attacks that once took days to complete in hours. The tool has been linked to numerous attacks targeting sectors including finance, government, technology, and healthcare worldwide, with some campaigns attributed to Chinese-speaking threat actors. The FBI and cybersecurity firms have issued alerts about Artex's role in facilitating rapid, multi-stage cyberattacks with minimal human intervention.

items.title: FBI warns hackers are using ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks on energy, manufacturing, telecom, and other sectors since August 2026 [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: The FBI issued a FLASH advisory warning that hackers have been weaponizing ARTEX, an open-source AI-driven autonomous penetration testing framework, to automate multiple stages of cyber intrusions including reconnaissance, initial access, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration. Since at least August 2026, attackers have targeted organizations across financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, and legal sectors, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. ARTEX uses specialized AI agents to convert high-level objectives into machine-executable commands, requiring minimal human input beyond initial instructions. Despite the original developer removing the GitHub repository in October 2026 after reports of malicious use, ARTEX remains accessible through forks, archived copies, and commercial versions. The FBI highlighted campaigns including theft of personal data from South Korean financial institutions and a supply chain compromise affecting over 2,250 downstream tenants via ConnectWise Cloud Backup. The framework lowers the technical barrier for complex attacks, accelerates multi-target operations, and exploits overlooked systems such as supplier portals and legacy services. It connects to external large language models including Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, and Chinese-origin models like DeepSeek, which is widely used by attackers. The FBI urged organizations to reduce internet-facing attack surfaces, strengthen identity controls, monitor application activity, and preserve evidence of intrusions to mitigate risks posed by ARTEX.

items.title: Google Labs launches Stitch Loop, an AI product agent that continuously monitors codebases and live metrics to suggest fixes and improvements with manual pull request approval [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google Labs has introduced Stitch Loop, a long-running product agent designed to help lean teams maintain and improve software after launch by connecting to codebases and live data. It identifies bugs, security issues, and performance bottlenecks, then writes code in a sandbox and opens pull requests for team approval to keep products optimized around the clock. Stitch Loop includes built-in loops for cybersecurity, latency, and accessibility, and supports custom loops tailored to specific goals. It integrates with GitHub and other tools, continuously learning from live product data to refine its suggestions while ensuring developers retain full control over changes before merging.

items.title: Why Anthropic's IPO Is Making Philanthropist Craig Newmark Hold Back on AI Safety Donations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Craigslist founder Craig Newmark says he's recently become worried about AI's potential to cause serious harm to critical infrastructure and human society. He's considered directing some of his philanthropic funding towards organizations trying to make sure powerful AI doesn't harm humans. But Newmark told me he is holding back for now because he expects a tsunami of donations from newly wealthy Anthropic employees to such organizations, following Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week. These potentially outweigh what he could give, and he feels his money could have more utility elsewhere. "Lots of people are paying lots of attention to it, so I can focus in other areas," Newmark said in a video interview earlier this month. "Now, maybe I'm being naive thinking that the people developing AI will be the most concerned about its safety," Newmark said. If AI employees don't donate to such groups, Newmark says he may have to call "very publicly and very loudly" for philanthropic support for AI safety in addition to his own.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects. My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox. To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations: external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly. external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance. external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package! Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code. The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running: I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. This external sandbox pattern provides a neat way to experiment with different approaches. Tags: sandboxing, security, ai, webassembly, generative-ai, llms, coding-agents, claude-code, codex, pi

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol OpenAI: We're introducing GPT-6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. I shipped LLM 0.38 with support for the new models. 6.2 Astra is 80% of the price of 6 Astra - $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output, the same price as Claude Fable 5.2 (which was also 80% of its predecessor). 6 Astra and Fable 5 were both $10/$50. The cached price is an even bigger discount - $0.40/million compared to $1/million for the older model. This is great news for longer running agentic sessions. GPT-6.2 Sol is the same $2/$10 price as 6.1 Sol and 6 Sol - which are half the price of GPT-5.6 Sol ($4/$20). Here are the pelicans for GPT-6.2 Sol and for GPT-6.2 Astra. The 6.2 Astra max pelican looks like this: I have a full comparison grid here, but here's how the high/xhigh/max pelicans compare with the previous Sol and Astra releases: I also ran my most recent benchmark prompt against the two models, using "Ultra' effort levels in the Codex CLI: Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data Here's Sol and here's Astra. Neither of them did a good enough job of morphing Yonkers into a big mech, at least in comparison to Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon. This video showing the Astra and Sol animations playing out at the same time: I created that video using GPT-6.2 Astra (Ultra) in the Codex desktop app by prompting: https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-astra-ultra/index.html and https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-sol-ultra/index.html are two videos of the same thing by two different models I need a video of the first 10 seconds where the top half of the video plays the first and the bottom half plays the second I need an overlaid label of "GPT-6.2 Astra" on the top half and "GPT-6.2 Sol" on the bottom half. These labels should be tastefully positioned. Make the video square and 2000x2000 pixels Then later: OK make it 20s Here's the exported transcript. The buzz around these new models is mixed at the moment. Astra 6.2 isn't scoring quite as high as Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks, and I've seen a few complaints that its communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne's review (in the form of a feedback letter he sent OpenAI during pre-release) has this useful example: When this model is working on long tasks, it can pull in a lot of subagents and manage them pretty well. It will then proceed to randomly ask you some weird internal implementation detail bullshit that you could not under any earthly circumstance understand, much less have input on. I sent "/goal make a new level for Outer Wilds". 2 hours in, it's "blocked" because it wanted to ask me "does r24's reviewer write it's clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4?" items.title: Anthropic IPO Yields 10X Returns for Venture Firms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: For the first two years of its existence, Anthropic was shunned by most venture capitalists, drawing instead on a mix of wealthy individuals such as former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and cloud computing companies like Google. But even after VC firms made relatively late entries into Anthropic, a handful of them, including Spark Capital, Factorial Funds, Sound Ventures and Menlo Ventures, will hold stakes worth over 10 times their investment when Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday at an expected $1.4 trillion valuation, according to people with knowledge of their investments. Slightly later investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners, are slated to see billions of dollars in returns.
